quizzes.title: Module 1 Quiz: Starting Out as an AI Automation VA

questions.text: What does an AI Automation VA primarily build?
choices: Workflows that connect apps so information moves automatically
Physical computer hardware
Legal contracts
Social media graphics only

questions.text: Why do businesses hire a dedicated Automation VA instead of building it themselves?
choices: Automation tools are illegal for small businesses
Building something reliable takes real skill, and a badly-built automation can cause real problems
Automation tools do not exist for small businesses
It is required by law

questions.text: What trait do clients look for most in an Automation VA?
choices: Speed above all else, skipping testing
Thoroughness in testing and clear documentation of what was built
Avoiding all client communication
Never asking clarifying questions

questions.text: Which phrase from a client is a strong signal of an automation opportunity?
choices: 'I love doing this task by hand'
'Every time X happens, I have to...'
'I never think about this task'
'This task is already fully automated'

questions.text: What is a reasonable minimum setup to start practicing as an Automation VA?
choices: An expensive dedicated server
A computer and free accounts on tools like Zapier and Make
A university degree in computer science
A paid subscription to every automation tool that exists

questions.text: What are the two basic parts of every Zap in Zapier?
choices: A trigger and one or more actions
A password and a username
A logo and a slogan
A quiz and a certificate

questions.text: What does a filter do in an automation?
choices: Stops the automation from continuing unless a condition is met
Deletes the automation permanently
Sends an automatic invoice
Changes the automation's color scheme

questions.text: Why might a builder choose Make over Zapier for a specific project?
choices: Make is always cheaper
Make handles complex branching and looping logic more naturally
Make requires no internet connection
Make cannot connect to Google Sheets

questions.text: What is one practical benefit of adding an AI step into an automation?
choices: It makes the automation immune to all errors
It lets the workflow think about data - drafting, summarizing, or categorizing it automatically
It removes the need for any trigger
It guarantees the automation never needs testing

questions.text: What does a tool like Chatbase let you do?
choices: Upload a business's FAQs so the chatbot answers using only that information
Automatically file business taxes
Design company logos
Replace the need for any human review

questions.text: What is a webhook, in plain terms?
choices: A way for one app to instantly notify another the moment something happens
A physical network cable
A type of spreadsheet formula
A chatbot's error message

questions.text: Why are Google Sheets and Google Forms often a good starting point for automation?
choices: They are the only tools that exist
They are free, simple, and work well as a lightweight database and data-collection trigger
They cannot be connected to Zapier or Make
They require advanced coding knowledge

quizzes.title: Module 3 Quiz: Core Automation & Chatbot Skills

questions.text: Why should you map a workflow before building it in Zapier or Make?
choices: Mapping is not necessary if you're experienced
It catches edge cases and missing steps early, before they cause a broken automation
It takes longer than just building and fixing later
Clients never want to see a workflow map

questions.text: What should you do before adding an action on top of a new trigger?
choices: Add every action first, then test everything at once
Test the trigger alone to confirm it reliably detects the right event
Skip testing entirely to save time
Delete the trigger and start with actions instead

questions.text: What should a chatbot do when it receives a question it wasn't trained to answer?
choices: Guess confidently and hope it's right
Recognize this honestly and offer a clear path to a human
Repeat the last answer it gave
Shut down completely

questions.text: What is a smart way to test an automation before going live?
choices: Only test with perfectly clean example data
Deliberately try messy, unexpected data to see if it breaks
Skip testing since the client will report any issues
Test only once, right before turning it on

questions.text: What should good automation documentation include for a non-technical client?
choices: Only raw technical code with no explanation
A plain-language summary, a simple diagram, and what to do if something looks wrong
Nothing - clients don't need documentation
A list of every other client's automations

quizzes.title: Module 4 Quiz: Building Your Automation Portfolio

questions.text: What is a 'mock automation project' used for in a portfolio?
choices: A real paid client project
A sample project built to demonstrate your skills before you have paid clients
A type of scam
A required legal document

questions.text: How should mock projects be labeled in a portfolio?
choices: As real client results with no disclaimer
Clearly and honestly as sample or practice work
They should never be shown to anyone
As guaranteed outcomes for future clients

questions.text: What is often the clearest success metric an Automation VA can show?
choices: The number of tools they own
Time and cost saved, shown honestly as a before/after comparison
How many hours they worked, regardless of output
The number of client logins they have access to

questions.text: What helps a portfolio communicate value faster than text alone?
choices: A simple before/after workflow diagram
A long block of unformatted paragraphs
Hiding all visuals
Listing tools with no examples

questions.text: Why should you document your process (tools, triggers, logic), not just the final result?
choices: It has no value to a future client
Clients want to understand how you think and build, not just see a finished automation
It is required by automation platform terms of service
It replaces the need for any actual skills

questions.text: What should an Automation VA resume bullet point focus on?
choices: Vague statements with no detail
Specific tools and quantified results, like estimated time saved
Only job titles
Personal hobbies unrelated to the role

questions.text: What makes a strong proposal for an automation-related job posting?
choices: A generic copy-paste message mentioning 'automation' in general terms
Personalization that identifies their specific repetitive task or bottleneck
Extremely long, unfocused paragraphs
No mention of relevant tools or skills

questions.text: Which platforms are commonly used to find Automation VA clients?
choices: Upwork and Onlinejobs.ph, filtering for Zapier/Make/automation roles
Only local newspapers
Random unrelated apps
None, clients cannot be found online

questions.text: What is a good goal during a discovery call with a potential automation client?
choices: Avoid asking any questions
Map their current workflow live and understand their real pain point
Immediately demand payment before speaking
Refuse to discuss their business process

questions.text: Why should you never list a tool on your resume that you haven't actually built anything with?
choices: It doesn't matter, clients never check
Clients in this niche often expect you to demonstrate real tool knowledge
Tools listed on a resume are legally binding
There is no reason, it is just a suggestion

quizzes.title: Module 6 Quiz: Landing Your First Client and Beyond

questions.text: What is a good first step when onboarding a new automation client?
choices: Guess what they want without asking
Get minimum necessary account access safely and confirm the exact workflow to build first
Immediately increase your rate
Avoid all communication in week one

questions.text: Which is a common pricing model for a single automation build?
choices: Per-project
Random guessing
Refusing to state a price
Charging only in a currency you don't understand

questions.text: Why might a working automation break over time even without you changing anything?
choices: Automations never break once built
A connected app can change its features, or a client can change their process
Only automations built incorrectly ever break
Breaking is impossible after the first month

questions.text: How should an Automation VA respond when a client reports something is broken?
choices: Argue that the client is wrong
Acknowledge it immediately, investigate methodically, then communicate clearly once resolved
Ignore the report completely
Delete the automation entirely without investigating

questions.text: What helps build a long-term Automation VA career?
choices: Refusing to learn new tools or platforms
Going deeper into key platforms, offering maintenance, and asking for testimonials
Never asking for client feedback
Avoiding all specialization
